name: Today
line: One page for your day, ready when you open the app.
how: Open the app and Today is the first thing you see. It pulls your day together from the other apps, so you can tick off tasks, open the notes for your next call, and turn meeting to-dos into tasks without leaving the page. Press Edit Today, at the bottom of the page, to add, move or remove tiles.
feats: A live clock, the next meeting with a Join button, and what's due
A sky behind your greeting that follows the time of day, with the sun or the moon in its real phase and today's sunrise and sunset
Weather for where you are, a city you pick, or your team's city, with the next 12 hours and 7 days a click away
Today's meetings with the call link, attendees and notes
For you: every comment where a teammate @mentioned you, with Done and Later
Tasks due today or overdue, ticked off in place
To-dos from your meeting notes that aren't tasks yet
Check-in questions waiting for your answer
A Getting started tile for a new teammate's first day, with steps that tick themselves
Calm background music while you work, off until you turn it on
Screen breaks: a calm reminder to look away every 20 minutes, over every display in the Mac app
Add tiles: starred docs, Dictate and clip shortcuts, people, recent files, a whiteboard and this week
Move and remove tiles; your layout follows you to every device
needs: Connect Google Calendar to see your meetings. The agent brief needs an Anthropic key. Weather comes from MET Norway, city search from Open-Meteo and place names from OpenStreetMap, all free with no key.

name: For you
line: Every comment where a teammate @mentioned you, in one list.
how: When a teammate writes @ and your name under a doc, a meeting note or a task, it lands here, newest first, with a count on the rail. Open one to read it in place, press Done to clear it, or Later to see it again tomorrow morning.
feats: Mentions from docs, meeting notes and tasks in one list
A count on the rail, and a For you tile on Today
Opening one marks it read
Done clears it until you are mentioned there again
Later hides it until 9 AM tomorrow or next Monday

name: Docs
instead: instead of a wiki or shared drive
line: Write in Markdown with a fast, source-first editor, or flip to a clean reading view.
how: Pick a space and a folder, write in Markdown, and flip to the reading view when you're done. Several people can work on the same doc, their edits merge when they save, and every save becomes a commit you can look back on.
feats: Team and personal spaces, folders and stars
A fast, source-first Markdown editor with a clean reading view
Edits from several people merge on save
Full history and saved versions, powered by git
Links between docs that survive renames and moves
Import Markdown, Word and HTML files
Download any doc as Word or PDF, in your team's fonts and colours
Present any doc as slides, with presenter view, speaker notes, a timer and a laser pointer
Draft a slide deck from a doc with AI, and download it as a PDF
Live task lists dropped into a page
Comments under every team doc, with @mentions that notify a teammate and wait in their For you list
Instant search across every space you can see
needs: Nothing extra. Docs works the moment the server is up.

name: Meetings
line: Jot a few notes during the call. Afterwards, AI turns them and the transcript into clean, structured notes.
how: Start recording from the browser, the Chrome extension in Google Meet, or the Mac app. Jot a few notes while you talk. When the call ends, Hotsauce writes clean notes from your jottings and the transcript, using the template you picked: a customer call, an interview or a stand-up.
feats: Record in the browser, in Google Meet, or any call from the Mac app
No bot joins your call
A live transcript, with speaker names matched to the invite afterwards
Templates for customer calls, interviews and stand-ups
Ask questions about one meeting or every past meeting
Comments and @mentions under team meeting notes
Voice notes from your phone
Import your history from Granola
needs: A Deepgram key for transcripts and an Anthropic key for the notes. Connect Google Calendar for attendee names and reminders.

name: Tasks
line: A fast task list that understands what you type.
how: Type a task the way you'd say it, like “Send the deck fri p1 #Launch”, and Hotsauce sets the date, priority and project for you. Or press Ramble, talk through everything on your mind, and pick the tasks it heard.
feats: Quick add that reads dates, repeats, priorities, #projects, @labels and +people
Recurring tasks that move to the next date when done
Inbox, Today, Upcoming, All and Done tabs, with your projects in the sidebar
Drag to reorder
Assign team tasks and attach files
Comments and @mentions on team tasks
Ramble: talk for up to five minutes and get a list of tasks
Reminders on your phone or computer when a task is due
Action items from meetings one click away
Import from Todoist
needs: Ramble needs Deepgram and Anthropic keys. Everything else works out of the box.

name: Dictate
instead: instead of a paid dictation app
line: Hold a key on your Mac, talk, let go. Clean, punctuated text lands wherever your cursor is.
how: Install the Mac app, hold the right Option key, and talk. Let go, and clean, punctuated text appears wherever your cursor is, in any app.
feats: Works in any Mac app: Slack, Mail, docs, the terminal
A warm glow around your window while it listens, with flames that follow your voice
Drops the “ums” and fixes “no wait, Wednesday”
Your word counts, time saved and recent dictations, kept on your Mac
A shared team word list keeps names spelled right
See which models hear you, keep your voice on your Mac if you like, and pick Fast, Careful or Off for the tidying
Voice notes on a phone come back with a title, summary and to-dos
needs: A Deepgram key for speech, and an Anthropic key for the clean-up.

name: Clips
instead: instead of a screen recording service
line: Record your screen and your face, and share a link instead of booking a meeting.
how: Pick your whole screen, a window or a tab, turn the camera on or off, and record. When you stop, you get a link to share instead of booking a meeting.
feats: Your whole screen, a window or a tab
Your camera goes into the video in a round bubble, whatever you share
A mic level meter before you start
Camera only on a phone or iPad, to record yourself talking
A shareable link the moment you stop
A read-only link for people outside, with the video, summary and transcript
An automatic transcript and summary for every clip
Speaker names, plus Summarize and Action items you can send to a doc or meeting note
Trim the start and end, or cut out a part in the middle, and undo it any time
Playback speed control for viewers
A shared library for the whole team
needs: A Deepgram key turns on transcripts, and an Anthropic key the summaries. On Cloudflare, clips are stored in an R2 bucket.

name: Ask
instead: instead of a separate AI chat
line: An AI assistant on every page that knows what's in your workspace and can work with your files.
how: Press ⌘J on any page, the round button in the corner, or type a question into ⌘K, and ask about anything in your workspace: “What did we decide about pricing?”, “Prep me for my next meeting”, “Turn this meeting's action items into tasks”. It opens beside your work and knows the doc or meeting you have open. It reads with your own access, answers with links to what it used, and makes docs, tasks and notes when you ask, each with an Undo.
feats: Named after your workspace, like “Ask Acme”
Searches and reads your docs, meetings, transcripts, tasks, notes, tables, links, clips and calendar
Reads the team chat rooms an admin picks (Ember, Campfire), never direct messages
Knows the page you're on, shown as a chip you can remove
Edits happen at once with Undo; deleting, moving, sharing or publishing waits for your Confirm
Your conversations are private to you and kept out of search
Admins pick the model and see each person's monthly use, with an optional limit
No web browsing: answers come from your workspace
needs: An Anthropic key, added in Settings. Sonnet by default; an admin can switch to Opus.

name: Notes
line: Quick notes and checklists on colored cards, for the things too small to be a doc.
how: Jot a note or a checklist, give it a color, and pin the ones you need often. Notes save as you type and sit on a board of cards, for the things too small to be a doc.
feats: Text notes and checklists that save as you type
Colors, pins and labels
Archive, trash and search
Move a note to the team space to share it
Turn a checklist line into a task
Import from Google Keep, colors and pins included

name: Files
line: Team files and your own, in folders, with previews right in the browser.
how: Drag files or whole folders in, then open them right in the browser. Search looks inside your PDFs, Word files, slides and spreadsheets, not just their names.
feats: Team files and Personal files, with folders
Drag and drop uploads up to 2 GB a file
Previews for images, PDFs, video, audio and text
Search inside PDFs, Word files, slides and spreadsheets
A Recent view of what you touched last
Share a file with a link your team, or someone outside, can open
Attach files to tasks
needs: Nothing extra on your own server. On Cloudflare, files are stored in an R2 bucket.

name: Tables
line: Trackers and lists with real spreadsheet formulas, kept as plain files your team owns.
how: Make a table or import a CSV or Excel file, name its columns and start typing. Formulas work the way they do in Excel, each column can be text, a number, a date, a checkbox, a choice or a person, and every change is saved with its full history.
feats: Excel-style formulas, worked out as you type
Columns for text, numbers, dates, checkboxes, choices, people and links
Sort and filter what you see without changing the file
Copy and paste with Google Sheets and Excel
Import CSV and Excel files, and download either
Team tables and your own, kept with their full history
Your AI tools can read and update them

name: Boards
line: Hand-drawn boards the whole team can sketch on at once.
how: Make a board and start drawing. Anyone who opens it draws with you live, and you see each other's cursors. Boards save as you go, and you can drop one into a doc.
feats: Hand-drawn shapes, arrows, text and images
Draw together live, with everyone's cursors
A laser pointer for walkthroughs
Drop a board into a doc
Saves as you go, in light or dark
A searchable list of every board

name: People
line: Everyone you meet with, gathered from your calendar and meetings. No data entry.
how: There's nothing to fill in. Everyone you meet with shows up here from your calendar and meeting notes, with your history together and anything still open.
feats: A directory built from your meetings, calendar and tasks
A page per person with past and next meetings
Open tasks with each person
A shared note about each person
Company pages grouped by email domain
Search across everyone
needs: Works best with Google Calendar connected.

name: Daily briefing
line: A five-minute audio briefing each weekday morning, made from your work.
how: Each weekday morning Hotsauce writes a five-minute briefing about your day and reads it aloud. Listen in the app or in your podcast app on the way in.
feats: Ready every weekday morning; Monday's covers since Friday
Today's meetings, with notes from the last time you met
What's due and which docs changed
A private feed for your podcast app
Speed controls, and the script to read instead
Make a fresh one any time
needs: An Anthropic key writes the briefing, and an OpenAI key reads it aloud. Without OpenAI you get the script to read.

name: Booking links
line: Share a link and let people pick a time that's really free on your calendar.
how: Set your hours, how long the meeting is, and a few questions. Share the link. People pick a time that's really free on your calendar, and the invite with a Google Meet link goes out on its own.
feats: Several links, each with its own length
Weekly hours with up to four windows a day
Buffers before and after, and minimum notice
How far ahead people can book
Your own questions, added to the invite
Times shown in the booker's time zone
Checks your Google Calendar and adds a Meet link
needs: Google sign-in with calendar access, and a free Cloudflare Turnstile key to keep out bots.

name: Forms
line: Surveys, sign-ups and requests for your team or anyone with the link.
how: Add questions, choose who can answer, and share the link. Answers land in Hotsauce, where you can see a summary, read each one, or download them all.
feats: Short and long answers, email, choices, dropdowns, ratings, dates and file uploads
Questions that appear based on an earlier answer
Team only, or anyone with the link
Close a form when you're done collecting
A summary, a table and a CSV of the answers
Post new answers to a team chat room
needs: Open forms for the public need a free Cloudflare Turnstile key. An AI summary of the answers needs an Anthropic key.

name: Sign
line: Send a PDF from Files for signature and keep the sealed copy next to the original.
how: Open a PDF in Files and press Send for signature. Add who signs, inside or outside your team, click where each person's fields go, and send. Each person gets their own link by email and signs with no account: they type their name or draw it. When the last one signs, Hotsauce stamps the fields onto the PDF, seals it so any later change shows, and saves the signed copy and an audit certificate in Files next to the original, and emails both to everyone on it.
feats: Signature, initials, date, text and checkbox fields, placed by clicking the page
Send to people inside or outside your team: each signs from their own emailed link, no account
Everyone at once or one after another, plus people who only get a copy
See who has opened and signed, make a new link, fix a wrong address, and read why someone declined
Copy a sent envelope into a new draft to send it again
Type your signature or draw it with a mouse, trackpad or finger
A sealed PDF (PAdES) that Adobe Reader and other PDF readers check for changes
An audit certificate listing each step, who did it and when, with the PDFs' fingerprints
An audit trail whose events are chained, so an edit to it shows
Envelopes are private to you; the signed copies sit in Files beside the original
needs: Nothing extra to sign: the server makes its own seal key. Emailing links needs a free Resend key; without it you copy each link.

name: Check-ins
line: A question the team answers on a schedule, like “What will you get done this week?”.
how: An admin picks a question and when to ask it, like Mondays at 9 AM “What will you get done this week?” and Fridays at 3 PM “What got done, and what's stuck?”. Everyone gets a reminder at that time in their own time zone and answers in a minute, typing or talking. Teammates reply under answers, and once everyone has answered, one short summary goes to the team's chat room.
feats: Questions on any days and time, starting with the two Basecamp classics
A push reminder and a card on Today when it's time to answer
Answer by typing or by voice
Replies under each answer
One summary to your chat room when everyone has answered, or at 5 PM
Answers are files your team can search, and your daily briefing and agents read them
Pause a check-in, or leave someone out
needs: Nothing extra. A chat room for the summary is added in Settings, and an Anthropic key writes the summary (without it, the answers are listed).

name: Links
line: Pages, PDFs and papers saved to read later, with a clean copy you, Ask and your AI tools can search.
how: Save a page from the Chrome extension, your phone's share sheet or the app, or add a PDF from your computer. Hotsauce keeps a clean copy to read, remembers where you stopped, and lets you highlight passages and add notes. You, Ask and your AI tools can search everything you've saved; share a link to give it to the team.
feats: Save from the Chrome extension, your phone's share sheet, the app, or an AI tool
A clean copy to read, or the page exactly as your browser showed it
Picks up where you stopped, with how much you've read in the list
Highlights and notes, with a Highlights tab across everything you've saved
Copy a page's highlights to a doc in one click
PDFs kept in Files with a readable copy of their text
arXiv, bioRxiv and medRxiv papers with their authors, abstract, version and DOI
Tags, search, and an archive for what you've read
Private by default; share a link with the team when it's worth it
needs: Nothing extra to save and read. An Anthropic key adds a short summary and tags to each page.
